title: Core types: outcome values, big-int quantities, Die construction
details: The foundation. An outcome value type following Python's rules (docs/semantics.md: bool is an int and merges with 1, str, tuple, float, Fraction; Python's ordering, raising on incomparable types). Big-integer quantities (pick the crate, note why in NOTES.md). A Die: sorted (outcome, quantity) items exactly as icepool's Counts keeps them (population/base.py, population/die.py __new__, collection/counts.py, creation_args.py). Wire encoding/decoding (harness/core/encode.py) in program/. Make the grammar nodes d, die, weights fuzz clean and mark them ported. Design the core so later tasks (arithmetic, map, pools, evaluators, PyO3, WASM) fit: read docs/ANALYSIS.md first and write the module layout you chose into NOTES.md.

title: Arithmetic and comparison operators
details: Die-die and die-scalar binary operators (+ - * / // % ** << >> & | ^, < <= > >=) and unary ones (- + ~ abs, round/trunc/floor/ceil), with Python's mixed-type semantics, bool-as-int, tuple concatenation, int/int -> float for /. Port binary_operator / unary_operator from population/die.py and base.py. Existing nodes add, sub, mul, neg, lt, ge: make them fuzz clean and ported. Add grammar nodes for every other operator, including scalar-on-the-left forms (3 - die), division by zero (raises), and float outcomes.

title: map, mixtures, Reroll; reroll/filter/split/clip/truncate
details: Die.map / icepool.map without repeat (map_tools/function.py, core_impl.py): callables come from harness/catalogue (named functions with a Python and a Rust side; start with ~15: add_k, clamp, read_roll from khepri, is_even, swap/tuple ops, ones that return a Die, ones that return Reroll, star-style multi-argument ones). Results that are Dice are mixed with weighted_lcm exactly (creation_args.py, math.py). Extra Die arguments to map (cartesian product). Then reroll (with depth and 'inf'), filter, split, clip, truncate, and the Die([die1, die2]) / weighted mixture constructors. Grammar nodes for all of it.

title: Repeated sums (@), explode, Again in depth mode
details: n @ die with int and Die n, _sum_all caching, the den**(max|n|-|n|) scaling (die.py). explode (which outcomes, depth, end) via the Again expression in depth mode (population/again.py evaluate_agains_using_depth): port Again as a closed Rust enum, depth mode only for now (count mode is a Phase S task). matmul node to ported; add explode and again nodes.

title: Pool, keep tuples, popping
details: Pool of mixed dice (generator/pool.py), keep tuples and their composition (generator/keep.py, highest/lowest/middle/slices/Ellipsis index forms), binomial popping with comb_row (math.py), skip collapse. Die.pool(), Die.highest/lowest single-die forms (die.py, population/keep.py). Sources should be enums with tiny hashable keys (see ANALYSIS.md). Grammar nodes for building pools and reading them through the basic evaluators once K6 lands (you can add the pool nodes now and port the evaluation in K6; nodes are only ported when they fuzz clean).

title: Multiset evaluation driver and built-in evaluators
details: The DP (evaluator/multiset_evaluator_base.py): backward algorithm preferred, forward fallback, order negotiation exactly as icepool does it (order.py merge_order_preferences, PoolSource.order_preference, UnsupportedOrder flips), room memo, multiple sources aligned on one outcome list, extra_outcomes, final_outcome returning a Die or Reroll. Built-in evaluators from evaluator/basic.py, keep.py, poker.py, comparison.py, argsort.py: start with sum, size, count, keep-index, highest/lowest outcome, largest_count, all_straights; add the rest as tasks if needed. Evaluators defined in harness/catalogue as named evaluators (Python subclass + Rust impl) for custom ones. Grammar nodes: pool.sum(), pool.size(), etc.

title: Multiset expression gaps left by S4d
details: Cases where the port says unimplemented (icepool-run and the facade's core path) while Python answers, all outside what the S4d generators produce: (1) multiset operators over tuple counts: an operator applied to a MultisetTupleParameter or a MultiDeal (e.g. map_counts / + / & over a whole hand tuple) gets tuple counts, which Python reduces with min/max/+/its function (often TypeError, not always); the core's operators take i64 counts only (operator/mod.rs `int`), and program/expression.rs refuses tuple expressions as operands (`binary_op` 'no multiset operand', `the_expression`). (2) MultisetMixture inners compared by hash_key: program/expression.rs `same_expression` compares generators, parameters, tuple items, mixtures and MultisetKeep, but two operator expressions of another kind over equal children are unimplemented (needs operator equality as `_expression_key`, functions by identity). (3) Keyword-only parameters of a @multiset_function (`def f(x, *, target)`) in the program language: mf_def has no kwargs, mf_call passes only `star`. Add nodes/generators for each, fuzz clean through icepool-run and crates/icepool-py/run-facade.sh, with fixtures.

details: FACADE-AUDIT.md lists what still runs in Python under ICEPOOL_BACKEND=rust with no task covering it: (1) expand.iter_cartesian_product (public) and cartesian_product / tupleize / vectorize over Decks, expressions or other outcome types (Python itertools.product loops); (2) Population.append / remove (Counter arithmetic) and to_one_hot; (3) Die.mean_time_to_sum (a Python recursion over core reroll/map/mean); (4) the Deck paths of zero / split and Deck.map's per-outcome loop; (5) evaluations whose sources the core does not recognise (user MultisetGenerator subclasses, operator subclasses without a spec) silently use upstream's Python driver: make that an explicit, documented host path or raise; (6) built-in evaluators over MultiDeal sources always go through host callbacks (tuple counts). Also tidy: dead module-level helpers in collection/vector.py, backend.py's out-of-date docstring. Pattern (see NOTES.md 'Python facade (S1)'): the facade module keeps its Python API and argument juggling; under ICEPOOL_BACKEND=rust its work runs in icepool_rs (no silent fallback to the Python code path), Python callables are host callbacks. Done when harness/core/upstream_suite.sh passes, crates/icepool-py/tests passes, any new grammar nodes are ported and fuzz clean through both icepool-run and crates/icepool-py/run-facade.sh (ICEPOOL_RUN=...), with edge-case fixtures.

title: Complex numbers: arithmetic on Value::Complex
details: Python gives a complex from `negative ** fractional` and then does arithmetic on it; the port returns Error::Unsupported (runner: unimplemented) for any arithmetic on Value::Complex (NOTES.md Gotchas). Found in S2: `die.standardized_moment(0.5)` with a negative deviation is `sum(p * complex) / sd**k`, a complex result in Python. Port CPython 3.13's complex add/sub/mul/truediv (`_Py_c_quot`, mixed float-complex arithmetic converts the float to complex first), comparisons (== only; < raises TypeError), abs, and repr (`(1+2j)`, `-0j`, `(nan+infj)`), bit for bit. Then let harness/grammar/die_extra.py `_moment_k` generate fractional k again (and any other generator that avoided complex), fuzz clean through icepool-run and crates/icepool-py/run-facade.sh, with edge-case fixtures.

title: JS facade: @multiset_function from JS functions
details: S6 built the JS API (crates/icepool-wasm/js) on the program layer: every method is a node called through program::call. Python's @multiset_function traces a function over multiset parameters; the JS API can only run one written as program JSON (MultisetFunction handles from mf_def). Add `multisetFunction(f)` to core.js: call `f` with parameter expressions (mf_var-like handles, tuple parameters for MultiDeal arguments, keyword-only parameters if S4f added them) and record the expression DAG and the evaluations the body returns (MultisetFunctionRawResult) in the core, as multiset_function.py's tracing does, nested calls included. Evaluations of JS MultisetEvaluator objects inside a body (program/host.rs evaluate() has no in_function/raw_result path yet) belong here too. Test: the JS fixture runner (js/test/fixtures.mjs) should route mf_def/mf_call through the JS API instead of program JSON; all fixtures/s4d multiset-function fixtures must pass that way, plus API tests against oracle values.

title: JS facade: the rest of the Python surface, and the JS tests in the gate
details: Left from S6 (crates/icepool-wasm/js): (1) `fromRv` with a JS random variable (an object with cdf(x): a host trait like program/host.rs HostFunction, mirroring harness/catalogue/rvs.py duck typing); (2) a `Wallenius` class (data -> deal(n) -> evaluations; node wallenius_deal runs it in one call today); (3) Die methods without a node: sequence(rolls), keep(rolls, index), mean_time_to_sum(target), stochastic_round as a method, map_to_pool / explode_to_pool / reroll_to_pool (after S3c); (4) a mapping (JS Map) as map/reroll/groupBy repl: today only the core's catalogue `mapping` (CoreFunction) works, a JS Map must become the program layer's Func::Mapping with Python dict semantics (key equality by Value, not JS SameValueZero). (5) The JS suite (`crates/icepool-wasm/js/build.sh --test`: every fixture through the JS API, API tests, tsc check) is not in harness/core/gate.sh, which the loop owns: ask in QUESTIONS.md / have the loop add it to the long gate next to 'fixtures through wasm'.
